name: Diy-Gid-Biy Cultural Landscape of the Mandara Mountains
description: In the Mandara Mountains of Cameroon's Far North Region, sixteen ruined settlements built of dry stone, without mortar, lie scattered across seven villages. Locals call them Diy-Gid-Biy, "Ruin of the Chief's Residence" in the Mafa language. They were probably raised between the 12th and 17th centuries by builders nobody can name. Around them, farming terraces, tombs and sacred places still shape the hillsides, and the Mafa people have lived there since the 15th century.
